final_rationale: The verdict did not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is substantively more careful than the original overbroad certification defense, but it does not cure the core compliance gap. The admissible evidence still shows: the HR benefits enrollment segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points; that segment is named in two employer rollout commitments; product's non-core framing does not resolve materiality on this record; legal review is still open; and policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Aggregate readiness and public risk-management/model-card guidance support process quality and a documented residual-risk posture, but they do not establish satisfaction of the controlling policy predicate. Because the unresolved issue is a live compliance condition rather than a mere drafting nuance, caveating the certification narrative is not enough to move this to compliant_with_caveats on the present evidence.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the HR benefits enrollment limitation was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the required disclosure was completed in the model card or launch record.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering this named launch use case.
The affected segment is named in two employer rollout commitments, which preserves materiality concern under the policy text.
Legal review remains open, so the disclosure predicate is unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and general governance guidance do not satisfy the specific policy requirement for material limitations in named launch use cases.
